# Step Counter Background Tracking Implementation
## Issue Description The step counter service was being stopped whenever the app was closed or moved to the background, preventing continuous step tracking. Users could only track steps while actively using the app.
## Root Causes Identified
### 1. Service Stopped on App Pause In `ProfileFragment.kt`, the service was being stopped in lifecycle methods: ```kotlin override fun onPause() { stopStepListening() // ❌ Stops service when app goes to background super.onPause() }
override fun onDestroyView() { stopStepListening() // ❌ Stops service when view is destroyed // ... } ```
### 2. No Boot Receiver There was no mechanism to restart the step counter service after device reboot, meaning users had to manually re-enable step tracking after every restart.
## Solutions Implemented
### 1. Removed Service Termination from Lifecycle Methods **File:** `app/src/main/java/com/example/syona/ui/profile/ProfileFragment.kt`
The `onPause()` and `onDestroyView()` methods no longer stop the service:
```kotlin override fun onPause() { // Don't stop the service - let it run in background for continuous tracking super.onPause() }
override fun onDestroyView() { super.onDestroyView() _binding = null // Don't stop the service here - it should continue running in background } ```
**Enhanced `onResume()` for Safety:** ```kotlin override fun onResume() { super.onResume() // Re-initialize sensors if needed if (sensorManager == null) { sensorManager = requireContext().getSystemService(Context.SENSOR_SERVICE) as SensorManager } if (stepCounterSensor == null) { stepCounterSensor = sensorManager?.getDefaultSensor(Sensor.TYPE_STEP_COUNTER) } if (stepDetectorSensor == null) { stepDetectorSensor = sensorManager?.getDefaultSensor(Sensor.TYPE_STEP_DETECTOR) } startStepListeningIfNeeded() } ```
### 2. Created Boot Receiver **File:** `app/src/main/java/com/example/syona/receivers/BootReceiver.kt` (NEW)
A new `BroadcastReceiver` that automatically restarts the step counter service after device reboot:
```kotlin class BootReceiver : BroadcastReceiver() {
override fun onReceive(context: Context, intent: Intent) { if (intent.action == Intent.ACTION_BOOT_COMPLETED) { // Check if step counter was enabled before reboot val app = context.applicationContext as? SyonaApp val repository = app?.repository val stepPrefs = repository?.observeStepCounter()?.value
// If step counter was enabled, restart the service if (stepPrefs?.enabled == true) { StepCounterService.start(context) } } } } ```
### 3. Registered Boot Receiver in Manifest **File:** `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
Added the BootReceiver declaration:
```xml <!-- Boot receiver to restart step counter service after device reboot --> <receiver android:name=".receivers.BootReceiver" android:enabled="true" android:exported="false"> <intent-filter> <action android:name="android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED" /> </intent-filter> </receiver> ```
## How Background Tracking Works Now
### Service Lifecycle 1. **Service Start:** When user enables step counter, `StepCounterService` starts as a foreground service 2. **Background Operation:** Service continues running even when app is closed 3. **Foreground Notification:** Persistent notification shows current step count 4. **Sensor Listening:** Service maintains continuous connection to step sensor 5. **Data Persistence:** Step counts are saved to SharedPreferences in real-time
### After App Close - ✅ Service continues running in background - ✅ Steps are counted continuously - ✅ Notification updates with current count - ✅ Data is saved automatically - ✅ When app reopens, current count is displayed
### After Device Reboot 1. Device boots up 2. `BootReceiver` receives `BOOT_COMPLETED` broadcast 3. Receiver checks if step counter was enabled 4. If enabled, automatically restarts `StepCounterService` 5. Step tracking resumes seamlessly
### Service Management The service is only stopped when: - ✅ User explicitly disables step counter in settings - ✅ User clears all app data - ❌ NOT when app goes to background - ❌ NOT when app is closed - ❌ NOT when fragment view is destroyed
## Technical Implementation Details
### Foreground Service Benefits - **START_STICKY:** Service automatically restarts if killed by system - **Foreground Priority:** Higher priority than background services - **Persistent Notification:** Prevents system from killing service - **Health Service Type:** Optimized for continuous health tracking
### Battery Optimization - **SENSOR_DELAY_NORMAL:** Balanced sensor reading frequency - **Efficient Updates:** Notification updates only on step changes - **Low Priority Notification:** Minimal battery impact from notification
### Data Persistence - Steps are saved immediately to SharedPreferences - Daily reset at midnight handled by repository - Step count persists across app restarts - Service reads saved preferences on startup
## Testing Procedures
### Test 1: Background Tracking 1. Enable step counter in the app 2. Verify "Tracking" status appears 3. Close the app completely (swipe away from recent apps) 4. Walk around and take steps (minimum 10-20 steps) 5. Check notification - step count should update 6. Reopen the app 7. ✅ Step count should reflect steps taken while app was closed
### Test 2: Device Reboot 1. Enable step counter in the app 2. Note current step count 3. Reboot the device 4. After reboot completes, check notification drawer 5. ✅ Step counter notification should appear automatically 6. Open the app 7. ✅ Step tracking should be active without manual re-enabling
### Test 3: App Kill 1. Enable step counter 2. Force stop the app from system settings 3. Walk around for a few minutes 4. Check notification drawer 5. ✅ Service should restart and continue tracking (due to START_STICKY)
### Test 4: Service Disable 1. Open app settings 2. Disable step counter 3. ✅ Service should stop 4. ✅ Notification should disappear 5. Re-enable step counter 6. ✅ Service should start immediately 7. ✅ Notification should reappear
## Permissions Required - `ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION` - Required for step sensor access (Android 10+) - `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` - Allows service to run in foreground - `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_HEALTH` - Specifies health tracking purpose - `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` - Enables auto-start after reboot
## User Experience Improvements
### Before Fix ❌ Steps only counted when app is open ❌ Step counter stopped working after closing app ❌ Had to manually re-enable after device reboot ❌ Lost steps taken during the day if app was closed
### After Fix ✅ **Continuous Tracking:** Steps counted 24/7, even when app is closed ✅ **Persistent Service:** Service keeps running in background ✅ **Auto-Restart:** Automatically resumes after device reboot ✅ **Accurate Counting:** No lost steps throughout the day ✅ **Battery Efficient:** Minimal battery impact with optimized service ✅ **User-Friendly:** Set it once, forget about it
## Files Modified 1. `app/src/main/java/com/example/syona/ui/profile/ProfileFragment.kt` - Removed service termination from lifecycle methods 2. `app/src/main/java/com/example/syona/receivers/BootReceiver.kt` - NEW: Boot receiver for auto-restart 3. `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` - Registered BootReceiver
## Files Already Supporting Background Tracking - `app/src/main/java/com/example/syona/services/StepCounterService.kt` - Already configured as foreground service with START_STICKY
## Known Limitations - **Battery Saver Mode:** Aggressive battery saver settings may still restrict background services - **App Battery Optimization:** Users may need to disable battery optimization for the app in system settings - **Manufacturer Restrictions:** Some device manufacturers (Xiaomi, Huawei, etc.) have aggressive task killers that may require whitelisting
## Recommendations for Users 1. **Disable Battery Optimization:** Go to Settings > Apps > Syona > Battery > Unrestricted 2. **Allow Background Activity:** Ensure app has permission to run in background 3. **Don't Force Stop:** Avoid force-stopping the app from system settings 4. **Keep Notifications Enabled:** The notification keeps the service alive
## Date January 5, 2025

# Step Counter "Sensor Unavailable" Fix
## Issue Description When the step counter was enabled and working correctly while the app was open, closing and reopening the app would show the message "Sensor unavailable" even though the sensor hardware was present and functional.
## Root Cause The problem was in the `ProfileFragment.kt` file's `onDestroyView()` lifecycle method. When the app was closed or the fragment's view was destroyed, the sensor references were being set to null:
```kotlin override fun onDestroyView() { super.onDestroyView() _binding = null stopStepListening() sensorManager = null // ❌ This was causing the issue stepCounterSensor = null // ❌ This was causing the issue stepDetectorSensor = null // ❌ This was causing the issue } ```
When the app was reopened, there was a timing issue where: 1. The UI update (`updateStepCard()`) was called through observers 2. The `determineSensorForPrefs()` method checked if sensors were available 3. Since sensors were null, it returned null 4. This triggered the "Sensor unavailable" status message 5. Only after this, `onViewCreated()` was called to re-initialize the sensors
## Solution
### 1. Fixed `onDestroyView()` Method Removed the nullification of sensor-related objects to preserve them across view lifecycles:
```kotlin override fun onDestroyView() { super.onDestroyView() _binding = null stopStepListening() // Sensors are no longer nullified here } ```
### 2. Enhanced `onViewCreated()` Method Added null-checks to ensure sensors are properly re-initialized if they were somehow lost:
```kotlin override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) { super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
setupStarAnimations() setupObservers() setupClickListeners()
placeholderPadding = binding.profilePicture.paddingStart
// Initialize or re-initialize sensor manager and sensors if (sensorManager == null) { sensorManager = requireContext().getSystemService(Context.SENSOR_SERVICE) as SensorManager } if (stepCounterSensor == null) { stepCounterSensor = sensorManager?.getDefaultSensor(Sensor.TYPE_STEP_COUNTER) } if (stepDetectorSensor == null) { stepDetectorSensor = sensorManager?.getDefaultSensor(Sensor.TYPE_STEP_DETECTOR) } } ```
## Additional Fixes While fixing the main issue, also resolved: - **AndroidManifest.xml**: Fixed missing `<application>` opening tag and removed incomplete `<provider>` tag - **HydrationReminderManager.kt**: Fixed syntax errors that were preventing the project from building
## How It Works Now 1. When the app is closed, only the step listening service is stopped 2. Sensor references (sensorManager, stepCounterSensor, stepDetectorSensor) persist as fragment-level properties 3. When the app is reopened: - `onViewCreated()` checks if sensors need re-initialization - Observers trigger UI updates with correct sensor availability - `onResume()` restarts the step counting service if enabled 4. The step counter shows the correct status: "Tracking" instead of "Sensor unavailable"
## Testing To verify the fix: 1. Enable the step counter in the app 2. Verify it shows "Tracking" status and counts steps 3. Close the app completely (swipe away from recent apps) 4. Reopen the app 5. Navigate to the Profile tab 6. ✅ The step counter should still show "Tracking" status (not "Sensor unavailable") 7. ✅ Step counting continues working correctly
## Files Modified - `app/src/main/java/com/example/syona/ui/profile/ProfileFragment.kt` - `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (syntax fix) - `app/src/main/java/com/example/syona/service/HydrationReminderManager.kt` (syntax fix)
## Date October 5, 2025
